comment: Verification contract for T-005 (medium, acceptance-first -- risk-gate-matrix.md's medium-tier row; tdd is reserved for high/critical), originally authored 2026-08-23 because T-005 reached Status: Implementation Complete (commit 472579a3, 2026-08-19) without ever being given this file. UPDATED same-day, second pass: the gap this contract's own first pass found (below) is now closed. Every field below is transcribed from tasks.md's own T-005 block (Risk: medium, Required Workflow: acceptance-first, Requirements: REQ-001/REQ-004/REQ-005/REQ-006/REQ-008) and reports/implementation/epic-193-a5-capability-resolver/T-005.md, never copied from T-003/T-004's own contract structure beyond shape-as-template. Every command this contract cites as evidence was RE-RUN against the current HEAD (febf7898, working tree with this pass's own uncommitted diff) rather than trusted from the implementation report: bash tests/resolve-project-context-match.tests.sh and pwsh -File tests/resolve-project-context-match.tests.ps1 both reproduced 59 passed / 0 failed, exit 0 (verification/qg/T-005/focused-tests-{sh,ps1}.log) -- grown from the first pass's own 37/0 by 22 new assertions (two new TEST-056 fixtures). requirement-traceability was performed manually and is NOT recorded as a contract check (medium tier does not require it; check-contract.py's RISK_TIERS['medium'] omits requirement-traceability), but its own findings are load-bearing and recorded in verification/qg/T-005/traceability.log. GAP CLOSED, NOT SMOOTHED OVER: this contract's own first pass found T-005's own Done When item 2 ('Byte-identity / aggregation / provenance locks') unmet because TEST-056 (AC-056, diagnostics[] warn/block cardinality) had no fixture, assertion, or reference anywhere in this task's own suite -- root-caused to a genuine, unimplemented production-code gap in resolve-project-context.py's own _write_evidence (hardcoded severity: 'block' unconditionally; contracts/resolver-evidence.schema.json's own severity enum already permitted 'warn'). That production code is T-004's own scope (Resolver Evidence assembly, REQ-004 share; tasks.md's own T-004 Requirements text names AC-056 among the production behavior T-004's own code must implement, even though T-005 owns the dedicated test suite) -- T-004 was Implementation Complete, not Done, at the time this gap was found, so completing a behavior T-004's own Goal/Scope already declared it owns is T-004's own completion work, not a reopening of finished scope or a frozen-spec amendment; T-005's own Out of Scope ('this task never edits resolve-project-context.{py,sh,ps1} itself') was not touched by T-005's own diff. T-004 extended _evaluate_capabilities/_write_evidence/_block (see T-004's own contract/report for the full account); T-005 then authored TEST-056 (two fixtures -- one reusing REQ-006 item (d)'s own existing dsl-warn-unmatched-trigger fixture verbatim, one a new multi-node fixture -- against the corrected engine, TDD RED->GREEN even though acceptance-first does not require it: verification/T-005/red-ac056-{sh,ps1}.log (55 passed / 4 failed, captured in an isolated git-clone scratch copy at this branch's own committed pre-fix HEAD, never reverting the real worktree), verification/T-005/green-ac056-{sh,ps1}.log (59/0). Two directional mutation kills confirmed in the same scratch clone: emitting a second summary entry is caught by the 'exactly one summary severity:block entry, never a second' assertion in both fixtures; collapsing the per-node warn entries into one is caught by the multi-node fixture's own 'exactly 3 severity:warn entries, one per outcome:warn node, never fewer' assertion (the single-node fixture correctly stays green under this second mutation). unit-tests and acceptance-tests are therefore now recorded passes:true, each with red_evidence pointing at this pass's own genuine RED capture (not the original, TEST-056-blind red-{sh,ps1}.log, which is retained untouched at its own original path for historical continuity) and green_evidence at the current 59/0 re-run. check-contract.py is therefore now EXPECTED to report this contract PASSED. regression (verification/qg/T-005/regression.log) re-ran: git diff --stat/status --short against plugins/ (empty -- T-005 is test-only and never edits resolve-project-context.{py,sh,ps1} itself, AC-032), git diff --check (clean), py_compile on the test driver (clean), the T-001 sibling resolver-evidence-schema suite as an incidental-breakage check (20/20 PASS), the upstream block suite re-run as a dependency-side non-regression check (141/0 both runtimes), and the FULL tests/run-all.sh/.ps1 sequence run detached with no deadline per this session's own explicit instruction: sh reports exactly 2 failing suite(s) (deterministic-lane-selfcheck.tests.sh, design-system-contract.tests.sh), ps1 reports exactly 1 (design-system-contract.tests.ps1 -- deterministic-lane-selfcheck has no PowerShell twin at all, a pre-existing structural asymmetry, not a regression this task's diff touches); both self-declare DESIGNED-RED for a documented pre-existing reason and match this repository's own standing baseline exactly, and this task's own new suite is confirmed registered and green inside that same full run. regression is therefore recorded passes:true. Stack: shell waives lint/typecheck/build -- this task ships only stdlib-only Python test drivers plus sh/ps1 dispatcher twins and no compile toolchain is configured for any of the three. check-component-coverage is correctly ABSENT (RISK_TIERS['medium'] does not name it at all -- unlike T-003/T-004's own high tier). task-state-check and check-workflow-state.sh (a separate, non-contract gate) were both independently re-verified and unaffected by this contract's own authoring: check-task-state.sh returns 'Task state check passed for 10 task(s).' exit 0, and check-workflow-state.sh both with and without --feature epic-193-a5-capability-resolver returns 'workflow-state: ok' exit 0 in both modes. Net: this task's own suite is a real, independently-confirmed, 59/0-passing artifact; the gap this contract's own first pass disclosed (TEST-056 unimplemented) is closed, not hidden -- both the closure and the closure's own evidence (RED/GREEN, mutation kills) are recorded above rather than a quiet passes:true flip.
